Subject: Post-demo next steps — model fit suggestions + rerank A/B slate

Hi Amelia / Lucas —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move from discovery to an evaluation: 

Recap (call takeaways)
- Primary goal: improve add-to-cart relevance and mid-funnel ranking for personalized search (mobile web).
- Key constraints: 95th-percentile latency requirement <= 180ms, PII-in-search concerns (no long-term token storage), and a desire to limit per-token spend in peak events.
- Important signals: session history, user segments, product popularity 

Recommended shortlist for model-fit evaluation
- Option A (low-latency reranker): redwood/rerank-lite-v1 — optimized for continuous batching and 8-bit kernels; expect ~10–12ms per doc rerank on p4d-like hardware (no KV cache).
- Option B (quality-first): open/llama-2-13b-8bit + redwood/rerank-head — higher NDCG, ~18–25ms per doc, better on long contexts and personalization features.
- Option C (quantized candidate generator + small reranker): redwood/candgen-4bit + redwood/rerank-small — cost-optimized for high throughput.

Prelim evaluation signals (we ran your sample slice against our internal bench)
- Candidate set: 150k queries (session-aware subset)
- NDCG@10: Option A 0.41, Option B 0.49, Option C 0.44
- MRR: Option A 0.32, Option B 0.38, Option C 0.35
- Note: these are initial, model-tuned numbers on MerchantLane sample; we'll re-run with your full prompt set. See attached eval summary for per-query strata.

Proposed A/B plan (sensible safe rollout)
1) Canary (week 0): 1% traffic to Option A (baseline) + logging of full traces (latency, token counts, rerank decisions).
2) Expansion (week 1–2): 5% traffic Option B + 5% Option C (compare NDCG/MRR uplift vs latency cost).
3) Analysis (week 3): evaluate metric lift on labeled holdout and business KPIs (CTR -> add-to-cart).
4) Fallback: automatic fallback to Option A if 95th-latency breach or error rate spike.

Ask / next steps
- Can you confirm: (a) legal can accept short-lived KV caches (we keep no long-term user tokens), (b) a 2-week window to wire up a 1% canary?
- Please upload any additional prompt templates or labeled holdout to the shared Drive link (I attached a starter prompt set we used).
- If you want, Marissa can run a short technical call with your infra folks to discuss rollout hooks.

Attachments: merchantlane_promptset_v1.json (prompt set, 18 templates), merchantlane_eval_summary.pdf (initial NDCG/MRR tables)

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Hi all —

Quick technical follow-up from my side (implementation + A/B ops):

1) Canary configuration
- 1% traffic routing via header-based switch (we'll give you middleware snippet).
- Full trace logging for canary: latency, token counts, chosen ranking, and a small labeled bucket (we can sample 0.5% of queries for human review).

2) Monitoring & regression hooks (recommended)
- NDCG@5 and MRR on the labeled holdout refreshed daily. Alert if rolling 48h delta > 0.02 NDCG or >5% MRR drop.
- Latency SLO: alert on 95th > 180ms for 30min window. Auto-fallback to Option A when breached.

3) Operational notes (to avoid quality regressions)
- We saw edge regressions on long-tail SKUs when generator options changed; mitigate with a hybrid approach (Option B for personalization signals + Option C fallback for sparse SKUs).
- Prompt hygiene: merchantlane_promptset_v1.json includes negative examples and guardrails. Please mark any prompts you want omitted before evaluation.

4) Next deliverables from Redwood (timeline)
- Today: upload full eval pack to shared Drive (done).
- Fri Aug 6: cost spreadsheet and rollout playbook (merchantlane_rerank_canary_playbook.md).
- Wed Aug 11: run labeled holdout sweep and provide per-segment NDCG/MRR with top failure samples.
